places.headline: Discrete — ℤ/6 ∗ ℤ/2

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ is elliptic: tr²/det = 25/81 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.82080422π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 49/20 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.42776179π. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 16/9 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.53544095π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 121/36 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.26173849π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Discrete — ℤ/4 ∗ ℤ/2
places.detail: Bass–Serre on the pair g₁, g₁·g₁·g₁·g₂: the bridge between the cores of g₁ and g₂ has length 0, and each finite factor moves its end of the bridge freely. The map from the Bass–Serre tree of ℤ/4 ∗ ℤ/2 to the tree is locally injective, hence injective, so the group is ℤ/4 ∗ ℤ/2 = ⟨g₁, g₂ | g₁⁴, (g₁·g₁·g₁·g₂)²⟩ with finite vertex stabilizers: discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 16/29 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.75776212π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 49/100 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.77236317π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 49/20 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.42776179π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 4/7 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.75324829π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 1/3 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.8135705π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

closure.summary: Γ fixes a point of P¹ and is non-abelian, but every generator acts on the fixed line by a root of unity: the closure is 𝔾ₐ extended by a cyclic group of order 2.
The generators are parabolic with a common fixed point, so Γ is unipotent: its Zariski closure is a one-parameter unipotent group 𝔾ₐ (conjugate to upper unitriangular matrices).
Γ is irreducible, not virtually abelian and infinite, so it is Zariski dense in PGL₂.

places.headline: Discrete — ℤ/3 ∗ ℤ/2
places.detail: Bass–Serre: the bridge between the cores of g₁ and g₂ has length 1, and each finite factor moves its end of the bridge freely. The map from the Bass–Serre tree of ℤ/3 ∗ ℤ/2 to the tree is locally injective, hence injective, so the group is ℤ/3 ∗ ℤ/2 = ⟨g₁, g₂ | g₁³, g₂²⟩ with finite vertex stabilizers: discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 25/7 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.21229562π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2² is elliptic: tr²/det = 25/147 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.86778276π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2²)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2² has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Discrete — ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/4
places.detail: Bass–Serre on the pair g₁⁻¹·g₂·g₁⁻¹·g₂·g₁, g₁⁻¹·g₂: the bridge between the cores of g₁⁻¹·g₂·g₁⁻¹·g₂·g₁ and g₁⁻¹·g₂ has length 0, and each finite factor moves its end of the bridge freely. The map from the Bass–Serre tree of ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/4 to the tree is locally injective, hence injective, so the group is ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/4 = ⟨g₁, g₂ | (g₁⁻¹·g₂·g₁⁻¹·g₂·g₁)², (g₁⁻¹·g₂)⁴⟩ with finite vertex stabilizers: discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ is elliptic: tr²/det = 1681/441 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.13919895π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 16/5 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.29516724π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 121/100 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.62925541π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 4/7 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.75324829π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Discrete — ℤ/4 ∗ ℤ/2
places.detail: Bass–Serre: the bridge between the cores of g₁ and g₂ has length 1, and each finite factor moves its end of the bridge freely. places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 1/9 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.89339924π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 28/9 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.31250562π. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 25/81 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.82080422π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2⁻¹ is elliptic: tr²/det = 9/14 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.73740061π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2⁻¹)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2⁻¹ has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ is elliptic: tr²/det = 64/25 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.40966553π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: |tr²g1·g2 − 4| + |tr[g1·g2, g1] − 2| ≈ 0.80769231 < 1. ⟨g1·g2, g1⟩ is non-elementary: tr[g1·g2, g1] ≠ 2 (no common fixed point) and neither trace is 0 (neither swaps a pair of points); a finite group would need an element of order ≥ 7 and so be cyclic or dihedral. Jørgensen's inequality then says ⟨g1·g2, g1⟩ is not discrete, so neither is the group. tr[A, B] ≠ 2 and the traces ≠ 0 are exact; the sum is compared with 1 in floating point (the value evaluated with 256 bits).

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: |tr²g1·g2 − 4| + |tr[g1·g2, g1] − 2| ≈ 0.80769231 < 1. ⟨g1·g2, g1⟩ is non-elementary: tr[g1·g2, g1] ≠ 2 (no common fixed point) and neither trace is 0 (neither swaps a pair of points); a finite group would need an element of order ≥ 7 and so be cyclic or dihedral. Jørgensen's inequality then says ⟨g1·g2, g1⟩ is not discrete, so neither is the group. tr[A, B] ≠ 2 and the traces ≠ 0 are exact; the sum is compared with 1 in floating point (the value evaluated with 256 bits).

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 4/13 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.82108762π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 36/13 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.37433408π. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 48/13 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.17891238π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 121/39 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.31413882π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 100/169 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.74866817π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 9/13 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.72684565π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 25/26 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.67378148π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: Bass–Serre: g₂ fixes one point of the axis of g₁ and moves both axis directions there freely and off each other. places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 50/13 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.12566592π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 576/169 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.25133183π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 729/676 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.65243703π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 9/5 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.53188428π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1²·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 64/25 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.40966553π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1²·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1²·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1²·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 64/25 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.40966553π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1²·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1²·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 4/15 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.83374203π. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2² is elliptic: tr²/det = 16/245 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.91843272π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2²)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2² has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

The map from the Bass–Serre tree of ℤ/3 ∗ ℤ/2 to the tree is locally injective, hence injective, so the group is ℤ/3 ∗ ℤ/2 = ⟨g₁, g₂ | g₁³, g₂²⟩ with finite vertex stabilizers: discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 1/6 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.86913075π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 9/5 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.53188428π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 16/5 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.29516724π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 16/5 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.29516724π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 45/13 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.23916155π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 20/13 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.57412424π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: Bass–Serre on the pair g₁, g₁·g₂: Fix(g₁) is at distance 1 from the axis of g₁·g₂, and g₁ moves the bridge freely. places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 9/8 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.644136π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 25/8 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.30983963π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 9/8 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.644136π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 9/8 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.644136π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Discrete — ℤ/3 ∗ ℤ/2
places.detail: Bass–Serre on the pair g₁, g₁·g₁·g₂: the bridge between the cores of g₁ and g₂ has length 0, and each finite factor moves its end of the bridge freely. The map from the Bass–Serre tree of ℤ/3 ∗ ℤ/2 to the tree is locally injective, hence injective, so the group is ℤ/3 ∗ ℤ/2 = ⟨g₁, g₂ | g₁³, (g₁·g₁·g₂)²⟩ with finite vertex stabilizers: discrete.

places.detail: Bass–Serre: g₂ fixes one point of the axis of g₁ and moves both axis directions there freely and off each other. places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 4/3 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.60817345π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 4/3 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.60817345π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 12/5 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.43590578π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 4/15 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.83374203π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 49/100 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.77236317π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 5/14 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.80682253π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 16/5 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.29516724π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 9/10 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.68537229π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 64/169 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.80088652π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 64/169 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.80088652π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 16/5 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.29516724π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 9/20 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.78225018π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 121/42 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.35480962π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 2/3 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.73227953π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ is elliptic: tr²/det = 1225/676 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.52994456π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 25/7 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.21229562π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2² is elliptic: tr²/det = 64/147 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.7859602π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2²)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2² has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1²·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 64/147 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.7859602π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1²·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1²·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Discrete — ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ
places.detail: Bass–Serre: g₁ fixes one point of the axis of g₂ and moves both axis directions there freely and off each other. places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: |tr²g2 − 4| + |tr[g2, g1·g2] − 2| ≈ 0.23809524 < 1. ⟨g2, g1·g2⟩ is non-elementary: tr[g2, g1·g2] ≠ 2 (no common fixed point) and neither trace is 0 (neither swaps a pair of points); a finite group would need an element of order ≥ 7 and so be cyclic or dihedral. Jørgensen's inequality then says ⟨g2, g1·g2⟩ is not discrete, so neither is the group. tr[A, B] ≠ 2 and the traces ≠ 0 are exact; the sum is compared with 1 in floating point (the value evaluated with 256 bits).

Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 1/6 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.86913075π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ is elliptic: tr²/det = 1681/441 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.13919895π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 4/7 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.75324829π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Discrete — ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ
places.detail: Bass–Serre: g₁ fixes one point of the axis of g₂ and moves both axis directions there freely and off each other. The map from the Bass–Serre tree of ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ to the tree is locally injective, hence injective, so the group is ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ = ⟨g₁, g₂ | g₁²⟩ with finite vertex stabilizers: discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 36/13 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.37433408π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 9/5 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.53188428π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 16/7 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.45437105π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 4/3 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.60817345π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 1/14 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.91467286π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ is elliptic: tr²/det = 81/196 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.79167399π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: |tr²g2 − 4| + |tr[g2, g1] − 2| ≈ 0.90909091 < 1. ⟨g2, g1⟩ is non-elementary: tr[g2, g1] ≠ 2 (no common fixed point) and neither trace is 0 (neither swaps a pair of points); a finite group would need an element of order ≥ 7 and so be cyclic or dihedral. Jørgensen's inequality then says ⟨g2, g1⟩ is not discrete, so neither is the group. tr[A, B] ≠ 2 and the traces ≠ 0 are exact; the sum is compared with 1 in floating point (the value evaluated with 256 bits).

places.detail: |tr²g1·g2 − 4| + |tr[g1·g2, g1] − 2| ≈ 0.39393939 < 1. ⟨g1·g2, g1⟩ is non-elementary: tr[g1·g2, g1] ≠ 2 (no common fixed point) and neither trace is 0 (neither swaps a pair of points); a finite group would need an element of order ≥ 7 and so be cyclic or dihedral. Jørgensen's inequality then says ⟨g1·g2, g1⟩ is not discrete, so neither is the group. tr[A, B] ≠ 2 and the traces ≠ 0 are exact; the sum is compared with 1 in floating point (the value evaluated with 256 bits).

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 9/121 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.91291689π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

The map from the Bass–Serre tree of ℤ ∗ ℤ/2 to the tree is locally injective, hence injective, so the group is ℤ ∗ ℤ/2 = ⟨g₁, g₂ | g₂²⟩ with finite vertex stabilizers: discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 1156/1089 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.6554713π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: |tr²g1 − 4| + |tr[g1, g1·g2] − 2| ≈ 0.1969697 < 1. ⟨g1, g1·g2⟩ is non-elementary: tr[g1, g1·g2] ≠ 2 (no common fixed point) and neither trace is 0 (neither swaps a pair of points); a finite group would need an element of order ≥ 7 and so be cyclic or dihedral. Jørgensen's inequality then says ⟨g1, g1·g2⟩ is not discrete, so neither is the group. tr[A, B] ≠ 2 and the traces ≠ 0 are exact; the sum is compared with 1 in floating point (the value evaluated with 256 bits).

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 2/5 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.79516724π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 81/44 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.52534688π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 36/11 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.2804378π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 36/11 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.2804378π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 36/11 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.2804378π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: |tr²g1·g2 − 4| + |tr[g1·g2, g1] − 2| ≈ 0.96590909 < 1. ⟨g1·g2, g1⟩ is non-elementary: tr[g1·g2, g1] ≠ 2 (no common fixed point) and neither trace is 0 (neither swaps a pair of points); a finite group would need an element of order ≥ 7 and so be cyclic or dihedral. Jørgensen's inequality then says ⟨g1·g2, g1⟩ is not discrete, so neither is the group. tr[A, B] ≠ 2 and the traces ≠ 0 are exact; the sum is compared with 1 in floating point (the value evaluated with 256 bits).

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 169/121 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.59753837π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 169/121 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.59753837π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 16/7 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.45437105π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: Bass–Serre: g₁ fixes one point of the axis of g₂ and moves both axis directions there freely and off each other. places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 9/11 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.70123081π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 16/7 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.45437105π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 36/25 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.59033447π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Discrete — ℤ/3 ∗ ℤ/2
places.detail: Bass–Serre: the bridge between the cores of g₁ and g₂ has length 1, and each finite factor moves its end of the bridge freely. The map from the Bass–Serre tree of ℤ/3 ∗ ℤ/2 to the tree is locally injective, hence injective, so the group is ℤ/3 ∗ ℤ/2 = ⟨g₁, g₂ | g₁³, g₂²⟩ with finite vertex stabilizers: discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 121/36 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.26173849π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 1/10 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.89891738π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 25/7 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.21229562π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Discrete — ℤ/3 ∗ ℤ/2

places.headline: Discrete — ℤ/3 ∗ ℤ/2
places.detail: Bass–Serre: the bridge between the cores of g₁ and g₂ has length 0, and each finite factor moves its end of the bridge freely. places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 4/7 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.75324829π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 16/5 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.29516724π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Discrete — ℤ/3 ∗ ℤ/2
places.detail: Bass–Serre: the bridge between the cores of g₁ and g₂ has length 0, and each finite factor moves its end of the bridge freely. places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 4/25 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.87181157π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 169/49 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.24207544π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 16/11 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.58792567π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 4/11 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.80501777π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 441/121 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.1926827π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 169/144 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.63558702π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1²·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 25/8 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.30983963π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1²·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1²·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 49/16 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.32172249π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2² is elliptic: tr²/det = 49/18 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.38239751π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2²)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2² has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ is elliptic: tr²/det = 625/784 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.70539139π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹ has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2² is elliptic: tr²/det = 8/9 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.68749438π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2²)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2² has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 1/9 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.89339924π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 1/9 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.89339924π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 9/5 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.53188428π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 1/52 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.95582291π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 10609/2704 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.088354171π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2·g1⁻¹·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 9/5 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.53188428π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 4/3 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.60817345π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 25/7 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.21229562π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g2ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1 is elliptic: tr²/det = 9/4 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.46010691π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.headline: Not discrete
places.detail: g1·g2 is elliptic: tr²/det = 25/8 is real and lies in (0, 4), so it rotates about its axis by θ ≈ 0.30983963π. A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has (g1·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 2; no such m has g1ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.

places.detail: |tr²g3² − 4| + |tr[g3², g2] − 2| ≈ 0.25017535 < 1. ⟨g3², g2⟩ is non-elementary: tr[g3², g2] ≠ 2 (no common fixed point) and neither trace is 0 (neither swaps a pair of points); a finite group would need an element of order ≥ 7 and so be cyclic or dihedral. Jørgensen's inequality then says ⟨g3², g2⟩ is not discrete, so neither is the group. tr[A, B] ≠ 2 and the traces ≠ 0 are exact; the sum is compared with 1 in floating point (the value evaluated with 256 bits).
